# package link

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/link"
```

Package link is the DNP3 data link layer codec (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 9): the FT3 frame format with its 16-bit CRCs, the control octet, the function codes and the addresses, and a [Reader](#type-reader) that reads frames from a byte stream and resynchronises after damage.

The package is a pure codec. The link layer procedures (reset of link states, confirmed user data with the frame count bit, link status keep-alive) run in the channel used by the client and the server.

It imports nothing outside the standard library and is useful on its own to analysers and test tools.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// Start0 and Start1 are the two start octets of every frame.
	Start0 = 0x05
	Start1 = 0x64

	// HeaderLength is the size of the header block on the wire: start
	// octets, length, control, destination, source and the header CRC.
	HeaderLength = 10

	// MaxUserData is the largest user data a frame carries: 255 for the
	// length octet minus the five octets of control and addresses.
	MaxUserData = 250

	// BlockSize is the number of user data octets protected by one CRC.
	BlockSize = 16

	// MaxFrameLength is the largest frame on the wire: the header plus
	// 250 octets of user data in sixteen blocks, each with its CRC.
	MaxFrameLength = HeaderLength + MaxUserData + 2*((MaxUserData+BlockSize-1)/BlockSize)
)
```

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrFraming is wrapped by every error that reports a damaged or
	// invalid frame. The stream itself is still usable.
	ErrFraming = errors.New("link: framing error")

	// ErrInvalidStart reports a frame that does not begin with 0x05 0x64.
	ErrInvalidStart = errors.New("link: invalid start octets")

	// ErrInvalidLength reports a length octet below 5, or a frame whose
	// length does not fit its function.
	ErrInvalidLength = errors.New("link: invalid length")

	// ErrCRC reports a header or data block whose CRC does not match.
	ErrCRC = errors.New("link: CRC error")

	// ErrInvalidFunction reports a function code the standard does not
	// define for the frame's direction (primary or secondary).
	ErrInvalidFunction = errors.New("link: invalid function code")

	// ErrShortBuffer reports a buffer that holds only part of a frame.
	ErrShortBuffer = errors.New("link: incomplete frame")
)
```

Framing errors returned by [Decode](#func-decode) and [Reader.ReadFrame](#func-reader-readframe). Each wraps ErrFraming as well, so a caller can tell a damaged frame (discard it and go on) from a failing transport with errors.Is(err, ErrFraming).

## Types

### type Address

```go
type Address uint16
```

Address is a link layer address. 0x0000..0xFFEF identify stations; the range above is reserved for the special addresses below.

```go
const (
	// MaxStationAddress is the largest address of an individual station.
	MaxStationAddress Address = 0xFFEF

	// SelfAddress is the self-address: an outstation that supports it
	// accepts frames sent to it as if they were sent to its own address.
	SelfAddress Address = 0xFFFC

	// BroadcastNoConfirm is the broadcast address (0xFFFD) for which the
	// outstations must not request an application confirmation.
	BroadcastNoConfirm Address = 0xFFFD

	// BroadcastConfirm is the broadcast address (0xFFFE) for which the
	// outstations must request an application confirmation.
	BroadcastConfirm Address = 0xFFFE

	// BroadcastOptionalConfirm is the broadcast address (0xFFFF) for which
	// the outstations may request an application confirmation.
	BroadcastOptionalConfirm Address = 0xFFFF
)
```

Special addresses (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 9.2.5.2).

### type Frame

```go
type Frame struct {
	// Dir is the DIR bit: set when the frame is sent by a master.
	Dir bool

	// Function is the function code together with the PRM bit: the
	// Primary* constants for frames that initiate a transaction, the
	// Secondary* constants for the replies.
	Function Function

	// FCB is the frame count bit of a primary frame.
	FCB bool

	// FCV is the frame count valid bit of a primary frame. It is set for
	// the functions that use the frame count bit
	// ([PrimaryTestLinkStates] and [PrimaryConfirmedUserData]).
	FCV bool

	// DFC is the data flow control bit of a secondary frame: the
	// secondary station cannot accept further data.
	DFC bool

	// Dest and Src are the destination and source addresses.
	Dest, Src Address

	// Data is the user data, 1..250 octets for the user data functions and
	// empty for all others.
	Data []byte
}
```

Frame is one link layer frame (FT3 format).

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (Frame, int, error)
```

Decode decodes the frame at the start of b and returns it with the number of octets it occupies. The user data of the frame is a new slice, not a view into b.

Every error wraps ErrFraming; a buffer that holds only part of a frame also wraps ErrShortBuffer.

### type Function

```go
type Function uint8
```

Function is a link layer function code together with the PRM bit (0x40), so that the primary and the secondary codes, which overlap numerically, are distinct values. It is the control octet without DIR, FCB/FCV and DFC.

```go
const (
	PrimaryResetLinkStates     Function = 0x40
	PrimaryTestLinkStates      Function = 0x40 | 2
	PrimaryConfirmedUserData   Function = 0x40 | 3
	PrimaryUnconfirmedUserData Function = 0x40 | 4
	PrimaryRequestLinkStatus   Function = 0x40 | 9
)
```

Primary function codes (PRM = 1): frames that initiate a transaction.

```go
const (
	SecondaryAck          Function = 0
	SecondaryNack         Function = 1
	SecondaryLinkStatus   Function = 11
	SecondaryNotSupported Function = 15
)
```

Secondary function codes (PRM = 0): the replies.

#### func (Function) Code

```go
func (f Function) Code() uint8
```

Code returns the four-bit function code without the PRM bit.

#### func (Function) Defined

```go
func (f Function) Defined() bool
```

Defined reports whether IEEE 1815-2012 defines f. The obsolete primary code 1 (reset of user process) is not defined.

### type Reader

```go
type Reader struct {

	// start and end delimit the unread octets in buf.

}
```

Reader reads frames from a byte stream: a TCP connection, a serial port or the payload of UDP datagrams written into a pipe.

It resynchronises after damage as IEEE 1815-2012 clause 9.2.9 requires: octets before a start sequence are skipped, a header with a bad CRC is skipped one octet at a time so that a start sequence inside it is found, and a frame with a bad data block CRC is discarded whole.

A Reader is not safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewReader

```go
func NewReader(r io.Reader) *Reader
```

NewReader returns a Reader that reads from r.

#### func (Reader) ReadFrame

```go
func (r *Reader) ReadFrame() (Frame, error)
```

ReadFrame returns the next frame.

An error that wraps ErrFraming reports octets that were skipped or a frame that was discarded; the Reader stays usable and the next call continues after them. Any other error comes from the underlying reader and is returned as it is: io.EOF when the stream ended between frames, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF when it ended inside one.
